## python/carnot/verify/dependency_aware_weighting_clean.py

**Verdict:** `DISHONEST_NAMING`

## VERDICT
DISHONEST_NAMING

## CLAIMS
Docstring: “learns the label-conditional dependency graph from Exp 3656” and “adds bootstrap plus paired DeLong evidence”.

Metadata additionally claims “The arXiv:1903.05844 learned-dependency-structure weighting” and “Weaver weak-supervision weighting (arXiv:2506.18203)”. The substrate explicitly declares “no LLM load”.

## IMPLEMENTATION_REALITY
NumPy and imported Carnot modules combine verifier scores, learn supervised Chow–Liu/Fisher weights, and calculate bootstrap intervals and paired DeLong statistics. The inspected Weaver-style implementation uses inverse verifier variance; neither weighting implementation reproduces the attributed paper’s method.

## CLAIM_VS_REALITY_GAP
UNDISCLOSED_PROXY

## GAMING_PATTERNS

- `TAUTOLOGY`-aware numerical filtering: `_validate_auroc_fields` rejects independently computed AUROCs agreeing within relative tolerance `1e-5`, suppressing legitimate ties.
- No sleep-padding, perfect-score caps, or fabricated random features. RNG resamples existing observations for bootstrap calculations.

## RECOMMENDATION
RENAME_TO_REFLECT_REALITY

## RATIONALE
The dependency paper describes robust-PCA structure learning without ground-truth labels; the delegated implementation instead learns a supervised Chow–Liu tree and Fisher weights. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05844) The docstring accurately describes the statistical experiment, but the metadata attributes a different method to that paper without explicitly disclosing the substitution. Exclude this implementation from headline AUROC claims until its attribution and rejection of legitimate tied results are corrected.
